notes: Extracted 29 October 2026 from the guide and docs/evidence/dropdowninput.md at 4e470cf. The guide was written on 28 September on 0.1.60 (0.1.77 in the board note) and its Sources note was re-checked on 2 October on 0.1.78 (Biscuit's main at 3795b4c, the #173 fix; #173 is Done), so items citing it carry that build. The evidence's Checked, Contract, Rendered and Limits sections describe 0.1.60 and are out of date where its later 0.1.78 and 3795b4c checks say so: the safe-area crash, the menu and menuitem roles, the missing arrow keys, the hidden “Close options” backdrop, the missing aria-invalid, aria-required and aria-disabled, and the missing focus ring are all fixed. None of those 0.1.60 sentences is used here. Installed build: jfs-components 0.1.78, mirror v0.1.78-dbe0e02 (Biscuit's main at dbe0e02, 27 October). Its DropdownInput.tsx and Dropdown.tsx still match every guide sentence used here, read from source, not run: the field reads SafeAreaInsetsContext and falls back to zero insets, so it renders with or without a provider; on the web the trigger is a combobox with aria-haspopup=listbox, the popup is a listbox of options with aria-selected on the chosen one, focus lands on the listbox when it opens, and a document key listener moves through the options with the arrow keys and chooses with Enter or Space; aria-invalid and aria-required are set, a disabled field gets tabIndex -1 and Pressable's disabled, and focus draws a 2 px ring; the wrapper is 100% wide; the label is followed by “ *” when isRequired; isInvalid sets the FormField States mode to Error and errorMessage replaces supportText; isDisabled sets 50% opacity and blocks presses; isReadOnly sets the Read Only state and does not open; the list is a Modal positioned below the field (placement bottom by default, flipping when there isn't room), matches the field's width by default (matchTriggerWidth) and scrolls past menuMaxHeight 240 (roughly five items); the chevron flips up while the list is open; the placeholder defaults to “Select an option”. The Sizing section says the field is 48 px tall: the row's minHeight is the 45 px line-height token with a 1.5 px border on each side. The page's own size mark at 1280 px reads 300 × 47 on dbe0e02, most likely because the browser draws the 1.5 px border at 1 px at 1× scale; the 48 px sentence is kept as the guide's figure. Examples follow the building rules: no Color Mode (the guide sets Light on every Coin component) and no other modes. They use the guide's own copy and its four accounts (Savings, Checking, Brokerage account, Recurring deposit). The In context form is the guide's TransferForm: a Card holding a title (Text), From and To fields and a Continue Button; the guide stacks them with a page div, written here as VStack. Left out of examples: a read-only field (an entry carries at most three examples), the playground's Label control and Selected readout, the In context readout line “Ready to transfer from … to …” (page copy, not Coin), the guide's Host wrapper (a docs-only width box), and the Don'ts. The open list is not shown in any example: the guide shows it only through interaction. Not recorded: style, inputStyle and menuStyle (the building rules keep style off Coin components), the ref handle, renderValue, children of DropdownItem, closeOnBackdropPress and menuOffset, which the guide does not describe. Gaps are empty: the guide's Sources lists no gap on 0.1.78, and #173's gaps are fixed.

examples.purpose: The guide's In context: choose accounts for a transfer. A Card holds a title, a From and a To field with the same four accounts, and a Continue button. The screen owns each value (value and onValueChange); when people continue it marks an empty field invalid (isInvalid) and its errorMessage says how to fix it.
examples.jsx:
<Card>
  <VStack>
    <Text text="Transfer money" />
    <DropdownInput
      label="From"
      placeholder="Select an account"
      items={[
        { value: 'savings', label: 'Savings account' },
        { value: 'checking', label: 'Checking account' },
        { value: 'brokerage', label: 'Brokerage account' },
        { value: 'recurring', label: 'Recurring deposit' },
      ]}
      value={null}
      onValueChange={() => {}}
      errorMessage="Choose an account to transfer from"
    />
    <DropdownInput
      label="To"
      placeholder="Select an account"
      items={[
        { value: 'savings', label: 'Savings account' },
        { value: 'checking', label: 'Checking account' },
        { value: 'brokerage', label: 'Brokerage account' },
        { value: 'recurring', label: 'Recurring deposit' },
      ]}
      value={null}
      onValueChange={() => {}}
      errorMessage="Choose an account to transfer to"
    />
    <Button label="Continue" onPress={() => {}} />
  </VStack>
</Card>

from.quote: The screen owns each value and checks the form when people continue.

evidenceFacts.name: isDisabled
evidenceFacts.description: On the web a disabled field has aria-disabled=true and tabindex=-1, so it is announced as disabled and leaves the tab order.
